summary: Junction readout achieves fast, high-fidelity transmon measurement by coupling the qubit to its readout resonator through both a Josephson junction and a capacitance, creating a nonperturbative cross-Kerr interaction with intrinsic Purcell protection. Operating a bifurcation-based readout on this architecture yields 99.4% assignment fidelity in 68 ns and 98.4% QND fidelity without external Purcell filters or near-quantum-limited amplifiers.
motivation: Dispersive readout of superconducting qubits suffers from Purcell decay and measurement-induced state transitions due to transverse qubit-resonator coupling, requiring additional hardware like Purcell filters and parametric amplifiers that increase system complexity and footprint.
method: A Josephson junction with energy $E_J^c = 4.01$ GHz is placed in parallel with the capacitive coupling ($J/2\pi = 83$ MHz) between a flux-tunable transmon and a $\lambda/4$ resonator ($\omega_r/2\pi = 7.66$ GHz, $\kappa/2\pi = 10.6$ MHz). The hybrid coupling generates a strong nonperturbative cross-Kerr shift ($2\chi/2\pi \approx -14$ MHz) while forming a lumped LC notch filter that suppresses exchange coupling and Purcell decay. Bifurcation-based readout is implemented by exploiting the resonator self-Kerr nonlinearity ($K/2\pi = -0.963$ MHz) induced by the junction.
result: At the flux bias point of maximum Purcell filtering, the device achieves assignment fidelity of 99.4% (68 ns integration, $\eta \approx 4\%$ quantum efficiency, maximum intracavity photon number $n_{\max} = 26$ for $|e\rangle$) and QND fidelity of 98.4% with critical photon number $n_{crit} \sim 60$. Purcell-limited lifetime $T_{1}^{\mathrm{pl}}$ increases by nearly four orders of magnitude as qubit frequency approaches the notch frequency, with excellent agreement between theory and finite-element simulations.
